newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis steady-firm, crush slows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis steady-firm, crush slows.

text.p: Rail and truck soymeal basis levels were steady to firm on Friday, underpinned by a slowdown in the crush pace, dealers said.
They noted, however, the crush may have to slow further during February if strength is to be maintained with export interest expected to decline as the next month progresses.

"February has always been known as a doldrum month. People are reluctant to pay a premium for U.S. meal when they know they can get South American within the next 30 days or so," one soymeal export dealer said, noting South American meal normally becomes available in late February or early March.
The weekly NOPA crush, announced Thursday, fell to 29.70 million bushels, down from 30.06 million a week earlier.
Dealers said the slowdown was mainly due to deteriorating crush margins, although cutbacks are not likely to be too severe while crushers' margins remain in the black.
The failure of soyoil prices to keep pace with recent strength in the soybean market has hurt margins, they said.
